content.text: Gabriel Carew ends his record after declaring love to Lauretta in Doctor Louis’s garden. His jealousy of Eric and Emilius leads him to spy in the woods; Eric is murdered, while Emilius’s innocence is revealed. Abraham Sandival then frames the story through letters, promising to explain Carew’s mysterious inheritance. In *Coningsby*, Coningsby courts Edith at Hellingsley, is rejected by her father, and later returns to London. Disinherited by Lord Monmouth, he studies law in the Temple, then wins election at Darlford through Millbank’s support and marries Edith. Meanwhile, Scott’s *Lady of the Lake* recounts Fitz-James’s journey through the Highlands, his encounter and duel with Roderick Dhu, and Ellen’s appeal before King James at Stirling. The closing essay reflects on self-conscious writing, social sympathy, and the difficulty of judging earlier generations.
